page: Amazon Web Services m8g.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an ARMv9-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The memory configuration consists of 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance's memory performance in the top tier, with a PassMark memory score in the top 10% and cached read bandwidth reaching 925.03 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong, ranking in the top 25% at 14.31 GB/sec. However, cryptographic operations are a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 25% at 1504.19. Large-model LLM prompt processing is also limited, with the 7B model prompt processing speed ranking in the bottom 10% at 15.42 tokens/sec, though text generation for the same model remains average at 10.76 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8g.2xlarge leverages the ARM64 architecture to deliver high memory bandwidth and balanced compute resources without the premium of x86 architectures. The primary tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage and weak hardware-accelerated encryption performance. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing.
